findings.problem: exp: em dash; and 'marketing shorthand today' denies the rule any legal force, when its ingredient rule for bottom-fermented beer still stands in Germany's beer law.
findings.fix: exp: dash removed; now says the 1516 text is long superseded but its rule lives on in Germany's beer law for bottom-fermented beer.
findings.source: Vorlaeufiges Biergesetz (1993), section 9, and the Biersteuer rules that carry the Reinheitsgebot forward

findings.problem: exp: offered Port and Sherry as examples of traditional terms; they are protected designations of origin, covered by the same EU wine agreements but not traditional terms.
findings.fix: exp: says Port and Sherry are protected names of origin rather than traditional terms, and that the same EU agreements cover both.
findings.source: EU Regulation 2019/33 (traditional terms) and the 2008 EU and Australia wine agreement

findings.problem: ans: em dashes, and the house-banned word 'practice' ('environmental practice'). exp: em dash.
findings.fix: ans: dashes to brackets and 'environmental management'; exp takes the site copy's dash-free wording.
findings.source: House rules (never the word practice; no em dash).

findings.problem: ans: em dashes. exp: em dash, the house-banned word 'practice' ('in practice') and American 'toward' twice.
findings.fix: ans: site copy's dash-free wording. exp: dash to a semicolon, 'in effect', 'towards'.
findings.source: House rules (never the word practice; British spelling; no em dash).

findings.problem: exp: said the metallic clash with oysters comes from tannin and oak, contradicting the bank's own iron lesson (a-0cdasvzc, a-9x83xbqa): the fishy, metallic aftertaste tracks the wine's iron.
findings.fix: exp: the clash tracks iron in the wine rather than its colour; oak and tannin only add weight and bitterness the oyster cannot carry.
findings.source: Tamura et al., J. Agric. Food Chem. 2009 (iron and the fishy aftertaste of wine with scallop)

findings.problem: ans: em dash. exp: em dash; and 'high-iron, tannic reds are the clash' put tannin back in as a cause, against the iron finding the same exp states.
findings.fix: ans: site copy's wording. exp: dash to a colon; 'high-iron reds are the clash, not reds as a class'.
findings.source: Tamura et al., J. Agric. Food Chem. 2009

findings.problem: exp: em dashes and en dashes; and 'so most Port and Sherry' in the 16 to 21% band, when fino and manzanilla at about 15% fall in the lowest band.
findings.fix: exp: dashes removed, ranges written 'to'; '(so Port and the stronger Sherries; a 15% fino sits in the lowest band)'.
findings.source: 26 USC 5041(b) wine excise rates

findings.problem: ans: em dashes and the house-banned word 'practice' ('trade-practice provisions'); one accept entry also carried 'trade practice'. exp: em dash.
findings.fix: ans: 'unfair-competition provisions' (the FAA Act's own heading for these rules), dashes to a colon and commas; accept entry reworded to 'federal alcohol administration act trade rules on tied house' (no word added, so no widening); exp takes the site's wording.
findings.source: House rules; FAA Act section 105 (27 USC 205), 'Unfair competition and unlawful practices'.

findings.problem: Key 'English West Country cider' for Herefordshire: Herefordshire is one of the Three Counties, not the West Country (whose PDO, West Country Farmhouse Cider, covers Somerset, Devon, Dorset and Cornwall); exp also filed Kingston Black, a bittersharp, under bittersweet apples.
findings.fix: Key option now 'English Three Counties cider' (position unchanged); exp names the Three Counties and keeps only bittersweet examples (Dabinett, Yarlington Mill).
findings.source: UK protected names: Herefordshire Cider (PGI), West Country Farmhouse Cider (PDO); Long Ashton cider apple classification

findings.problem: ans: 'Poire Domfront' drops the accent that makes it perry (poiré) rather than pear. exp: em dash; and 'demands a majority of Plant de Blanc' overstates the rule, which is at least 40 per cent in the blend.
findings.fix: ans: 'Poiré Domfront'. exp: dash removed; 'demands at least 40 per cent Plant de Blanc in the blend'.
findings.source: INAO, Domfront specification (PNO2025 documents; minimum 40% Plant de Blanc in the blend)

findings.problem: exp: named an option by position ('option 4', which the option re-deal makes wrong and the option_reference regex misses because it is a digit); said the 60% figure reappears only at Tokubetsu Junmai, when Junmai Ginjo also needs 60% or lower; and two spaced hyphens used as dashes.
findings.fix: exp: the option is named by its content (the 30% polishing requirement as the pre-2004 rule); 'The 60% figure returns at Junmai Ginjo and Tokubetsu Junmai'; spaced hyphens removed.
findings.source: National Tax Agency, Seishu no seiho hinshitsu hyoji kijun (tokutei meishoshu table)
